Jensen/supporting-line equality requires constant integer lambda. Gram-spectrum argument identifies symmetric 2-designs. Vandermonde gives a full exact nonnegative incidence-biclique defect, strictly detecting nonplanes. The logarithmic expansion of exact binomial ratios yields e^-1-(5/2)e^-2 along prime-power plane orders. An embedded standard-library checker independently enumerated exact rational examples and passed 39 assertions; it is supplementary, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The precise statistic is the variance of the zero-path multiplicity count after two uniformly permuted regular graph layers. Chiclana (2026) proves an expected quadratic norm determined by d and r, but two kernels with the same d=7,r=3 have distinct zero-count variances 4/25 and 48/175; thus the source theorem cannot determine the claimed observable. Cameron–Soicher (2007) gives general intersection-count identities, but the inspected material does not supply the sharp stochastic variance optimum, exact nonnegative biclique defect, or prime-power asymptotic constant. Targeted research-record searches of source, aliases, projective-plane equality and four-cycle terms found related design and occupancy records but no stronger exact implication. Novelty is a best-knowledge self-review; broad historical design-optimality results may subsume some components.
residual_risks: Historical convex design optimality theorems may implicitly subsume the strict-integer-overlap extremal step; exact historical priority awaits independent review.

value.rationale: The motivating source identifies empirical Poisson occupancy at the first critical two-layer scale but its expected chi-square invariant cannot distinguish graph geometry. This theorem identifies the precise variance observable, its full extremal equality class, a strictly positive motif-by-motif structural stability defect, and the sharp variance-density constant along an infinite family of nontrivial graph geometries. It reveals substantial lower fluctuations hidden by the universal first-order Poisson law. A natural meaningful complete classification is obtained for integer lambda with feasible symmetric designs, without claims beyond that domain.
